# Summary

This report analyses day-ahead electricity prices
across the European bidding zones. The analysis uses data retrieved from the ENTSO-E
Transparency Platform and focuses on the most recent
7 days of available market data.


```{python}
# Import libs
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown, HTML, display 

PROJECT_ROOT = Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT / "src"))

from market_data import load_day_ahead_data
from market_analysis import (
    calculate_market_statistics,
    calculate_hourly_patterns,
    calculate_daily_prices,
    identify_price_extremes,
    generate_executive_summary,
)
```


```{python}
# Logging config
from logging_config import setup_logging
logger = setup_logging()
```


# Day-Ahead Market


## Overview

```{python}
# Retrieve the most recent seven days of data
prices_long = load_day_ahead_data(days=7)
```

```{python}
# Market analysis
market_stats = calculate_market_statistics(prices_long)
hourly_patterns = calculate_hourly_patterns(prices_long)
daily_prices = calculate_daily_prices(prices_long)
price_extremes = identify_price_extremes(prices_long)
```

```{python}
# Clean the data for KPI calculations
kpi_data = prices_long.copy()
kpi_data["price"] = pd.to_numeric(kpi_data["price"], errors="coerce")
kpi_data["timestamp"] = pd.to_datetime(
    kpi_data["timestamp"], errors="coerce"
)

kpi_data = kpi_data.dropna(subset=["price", "timestamp"])

# KPI calculations
average_price = kpi_data["price"].mean()

highest_idx = kpi_data["price"].idxmax()
lowest_idx = kpi_data["price"].idxmin()

highest_row = kpi_data.loc[highest_idx]
lowest_row = kpi_data.loc[lowest_idx]

highest_price = highest_row["price"]
highest_zone = highest_row["bidding_zone"]
highest_time = highest_row["timestamp"]

lowest_price = lowest_row["price"]
lowest_zone = lowest_row["bidding_zone"]
lowest_time = lowest_row["timestamp"]

negative_count = int((kpi_data["price"] < 0).sum())
negative_pct = negative_count / len(kpi_data) * 100

# Formatting
average_price_text = f"{average_price:,.2f}"
highest_price_text = f"{highest_price:,.2f}"
lowest_price_text = f"{lowest_price:,.2f}"

highest_time_text = highest_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
lowest_time_text = lowest_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
```

```{python}
# Create an interactive line chart.
fig = px.line(
    prices_long,
    x="timestamp",
    y="price",
    color="bidding_zone",
    title="Day-Ahead Electricity Prices by Bidding Zone",
    labels={
        "timestamp": "Date and time",
        "price": "Price (€/MWh)",
        "bidding_zone": "Bidding zone",
    },
    template="plotly_white",
)

# Improve chart layout.
fig.update_layout(
    hovermode="x unified",
    legend_title_text="Bidding zone",
    xaxis_title="Date and time",
    yaxis_title="Electricity price (EUR/MWh)",
)

fig.update_traces(
    line=dict(width=2),
)

# Display the chart.
fig.show()
```

## Patterns
```{python}
# Daily
daily_prices = calculate_daily_prices(prices_long)

fig = px.line(
    daily_prices,
    x="date",
    y="mean_price",
    color="bidding_zone",
    title="Daily Average Day-Ahead Electricity Prices",
    labels={
        "date": "Date",
        "mean_price": "Average Price (€/MWh)",
        "bidding_zone": "Bidding Zone",
    },
)

fig.show()

# Hourly
hourly_patterns = calculate_hourly_patterns(prices_long)

# Ensure all 24 hours are represented
all_hours = pd.DataFrame({"hour": range(24)})

zones = hourly_patterns["bidding_zone"].unique()

hourly_patterns = (
    pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
        [zones, range(24)],
        names=["bidding_zone", "hour"]
    )
    .to_frame(index=False)
    .merge(hourly_patterns, on=["bidding_zone", "hour"], how="left")
)

fig = px.line(
    hourly_patterns,
    x="hour",
    y="mean_price",
    color="bidding_zone",
    markers=True,
    title="Average Day-Ahead Price by Hour",
    labels={
        "hour": "Hour of Day",
        "mean_price": "Average Price (€/MWh)",
        "bidding_zone": "Bidding Zone",
    },
)

fig.update_xaxes(
    tickmode="linear",
    tick0=0,
    dtick=1,
    range=[0, 23]
)

fig.show()


# Price extremes
extremes = identify_price_extremes(prices_long)

display(extremes)
```
